answer: Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the nadir checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. The shale graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the sparrow audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 5 times its size, so a group of 49 keys loses far more than 49 single identities would. That is 39 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
